$comment: Module map for agent/src and cli/src (round 3 TRAIN 1 landed: directory now equals module). issue #3493: this is the single per-path {module, layer} source -- at its retirement, tools/layers.json's hand-maintained path=>layer map was proven to equal this file's per-module `layer` expanded over `files` (zero mismatches over the then-225 agent/src files); sandbox/tests/offline/guards/regress_agent_src_requires.php's directional layer lint now derives its file=>layer map from here directly. `layer_notes` carries layers.json's old free-text rationale for placements a filename suffix would suggest otherwise (e.g. a *Materializer file classified repository, not engine).
rules: Every file under a root belongs to exactly one module directory.

A module has exactly one layer; that is what lets sandbox/tests/offline/guards/regress_agent_src_requires.php's directional layer lint derive each file's layer straight from here instead of a second, separately hand-maintained tools/layers.json (issue #3493).

Within a root, a module may reference only modules in a strictly lower layer, plus itself; every same-layer or upward edge that exists today is listed in that module's `exceptions` and is a ratchet (may shrink, never grow).
cli modules may reference agent modules named in `depends_on` (written `agent:<Module>`); the agent root must never reference cli.
`entry_points` are the classes other modules already reference; a new cross-module reference to a non-entry-point class is a design change, not a refactor.

Namespaces do not change in this move: agent/src stays `namespace WPrism;`, cli/src stays `namespace WPrism\Orchestrator;`. The additive classmap (agent/wprism-classmap.php, cli/wprism-classmap.php) maps FQCN to path, so directory != namespace is legal. Sub-namespaces migrate later, per module, Kernel first.

A reserved (0-file) module carries no `exceptions`: composition across engine modules happens in the surface module (`cli/src/Command/`, `agent/src/Command/`), which is where every verb boundary class lives. The one designed exception is a surface->surface dispatch edge the ladder cannot avoid (agent Command -> Assess); when a reserved module lands, any exception it actually needs is a reviewed map change, not a pre-authorised budget.

layer_notes.src/Apply/TypedTableMaterializer.php: Engine with the rest of the *Materializer family, for the same reason as TypedTableCapture.
layer_notes.src/Assess/AssessInventory.php: Surface with Cli.php: the read-only assess projection (round-3 MUP §4.5) is a command-shaped composition over policy, adapter and review, reached only from the wp wprism verb that publishes it.
layer_notes.src/Capture/TypedTableCapture.php: Engine with the rest of the *Capture family even though it only reads kernel files; the recorded Snapshot -> TypedTableCapture edge names the real seam (a repository state model driving engine capture) instead of hiding it behind a convenient placement.
layer_notes.src/Code/CodeMaterializer.php: Repository, not engine, despite the *Materializer suffix: it depends only on PathSafety and is used solely by Code. The engine *Materializer family materializes authored state; this one materializes code bytes for the repository half.
layer_notes.src/Code/CodeOwnershipPruner.php: Repository for the same reason as CodeMaterializer: a Code-owned pruner over PathSafety, not an engine apply step.
layer_notes.src/Code/CodeStageTransaction.php: Repository: a Code-owned Db/Ledger transaction, kept with Code so the code half stays internally consistent.
layer_notes.src/Command/Cli.php: A surface file, and the top of the ladder: it may reference anything.
layer_notes.src/Grammar/Blocks.php: Policy, not kernel: block markup rewriting is driven by Policy and Tokens. Kept in one layer with Tokens/Shortcodes so the codec cycle resolves inside a layer instead of across two.
Policy with Tokens/Shortcodes: it registers policy-declared shortcode alternates.
layer_notes.src/Grammar/Shortcodes.php: Policy with Tokens/Blocks, for the same reason as Blocks.
layer_notes.src/Grammar/Tokens.php: Policy, not kernel, although the four codecs it composes (TextTokenizer, IdentityTokenCodec, StructuredReferenceCodec, UrlQueryReferenceCodec) are kernel: Tokens itself reads Policy to decide what a reference means. Its read of Ledger is the recorded inversion.
layer_notes.src/Kernel/Canon.php: Kernel by doctrine (canonical JSON/ordering is a primitive). Its single read of Policy is the oldest recorded inversion in the graph and the highest-value one to retire.
layer_notes.src/Kernel/DurableFilesystem.php: Kernel by doctrine. Its two upward edges to Publish/PublicationJournal are an artefact of the guarded InitialStateBoundaryException class being declared in three files; the scanner attributes a reference to every declaring file. Recorded rather than hidden, because collapsing that triple declaration is the real fix.
layer_notes.src/Kernel/OptionState.php: Kernel: it depends on Canon alone and is read by 26 files across every layer, including policy grammars. Placing it any higher would invert the *Grammar reads without describing anything true.
layer_notes.src/Kernel/ReferenceKeyspaceGrammar.php: Kernel with the rest of the reference grammar: it depends only on ReferenceRules, and the policy loader that reads it sits above.
layer_notes.src/Kernel/ReferenceScopeClassifier.php: Kernel: a dependency-free classifier read by Tokens, Shortcodes, Blocks and Capture.
layer_notes.src/Kernel/ReferenceShapeGrammar.php: Kernel with the rest of the reference grammar (ReferenceRules only).
layer_notes.src/Kernel/TableGraph.php: Kernel: a dependency-free table dependency graph.
layer_notes.src/Kernel/UserMetaState.php: Kernel: a dependency-free state model, read from the repository and engine layers.
layer_notes.src/Policy/ArtifactPolicyIdentity.php: Policy, not adapter: it is the identity a policy load stamps onto a compiled artifact. Its read of AdapterSources is the recorded inversion, not a reason to promote the file.
layer_notes.src/Policy/CodeConfigGrammar.php: Policy (the *Grammar axis) although it validates a Code envelope: its caller is SitePolicyValidator/Policy. The resulting read of Code is recorded rather than resolved by moving the grammar into the repository layer.
layer_notes.src/Policy/DeletionCapabilityResolver.ph: Policy (the *Resolver axis), not the Deletion* engine family: it answers a policy question from OptionNameReferenceResolver and is read by Policy itself.
layer_notes.src/Repository/CanonicalSurfaces.php: Repository: a catalogue over OptionState and SidebarState, so it sits with the state models it enumerates rather than with the planners that consume it.
layer_notes.src/Repository/Identity.php: Repository: identity is repository-side truth (Uuid + SidebarState + Canon), not an engine operation.
layer_notes.src/Repository/IdentityBackup.php: Repository with the rest of the Identity* family. It reads only policy/repository/kernel files, so the placement costs nothing.
layer_notes.src/Repository/ReferenceGraph.php: Repository, unlike the Reference* grammar/rules/path files: it is a graph over Snapshot and SidebarState, i.e. compiled repository state.
Repository with the Repository* family. Its read of the engine Deletion model is a real inversion and is recorded: the parser should take a deletion shape, not the engine type.
layer_notes.src/Repository/SidebarState.php: Repository: a state model over Ledger/Snapshot/Db, the same axis as Snapshot and OptionState consumers.
layer_notes.src/Repository/StateTreeWalker.php: Repository: a dependency-free walker over compiled state trees, read by Lint.

Kernel.purpose: Dependency-free primitives — canonical JSON, database access, reference codecs, durable filesystem, side-effect guards, identifiers, secrets and PII redaction — that everything else is built on.

Policy.purpose: Loads, validates and pins the manifest and site policy that decides which WordPress state WPrism owns, and answers every ownership question the engine asks.

Grammar.purpose: Declarative grammars and resolvers that turn manifest declarations and WordPress content syntax (blocks, shortcodes, tokens, options, taxonomies, user meta) into typed policy structures.

Repository.purpose: The durable repository of owned state: compiled artifacts, identity registry, ledger, provenance journal, reference graph, snapshots and their validators.

Code.purpose: Ownership, staging, compatibility and materialization of code artifacts (themes, plugins, mu-plugins) as repository state.

Capture.purpose: Reads owned state out of a live site into repository shape behind safety gates, a capture identity and a capture transaction.

Apply.purpose: Plans, executes and verifies writes of repository state into a live site: apply planning, services, the authored transaction, convergence verification and the per-entity materializers.

Scope.purpose: Scoped (partial-site) execution — the state overlay, session and work projection that let apply and capture run over a subset of the repository.

Rebuild.purpose: Derived-state regeneration: negotiating, selecting and dispatching native or provider rebuild actions after a write.

Publication.purpose: Atomic publication of a state tree to disk plus the journal that makes an interrupted publication recoverable.

Promotion.purpose: Deploy, lifecycle and promotion mechanics — planners, leases, locks, externally-authorized repository binding, session journals and state handoff between environments.

Recovery.purpose: Target-local retained-checkpoint protection: streaming authenticated encryption and authenticated-before-output restore over operator-directed database evidence.

Delete.purpose: Deletion authority, deletion guards, orphan repair and the executors that remove owned entities and record tombstones.

Init.purpose: First-contact onboarding of a site: probing, planning, confirming, journalling and recovering the initial owned baseline.

Review.purpose: Read-only projections over plans and state — lint and its reference scanners, coverage, pending, effect-declaration coverage and plan explanation.

Adapter.purpose: The plugin-facing boundary: manifest sources, adapter registry, observation, site adapter certification and the provider SDK the engine calls through.

Command.purpose: The `wp wprism …` WP-CLI surface: verb dispatch, argument parsing, refusal envelopes and operator output.

exceptions.reason: designed: Command dispatches the Assess projections; the reverse edge is forbidden.

Assess.purpose: Read-only inventory and projection commands answering 'what is here, and what can WPrism do with it' before any write.

Transport.purpose: Carries bytes and commands to a target environment: the transport implementations, the environment driver handle, version-independent recovery fence and code deployment.

Plan.purpose: The plan wire contract and its operator/JSON renderings, with no I/O of its own, plus `HumanViewLimit` -- the one `--limit=<1..200>` grammar and `N more (use --format=json)` tail every human view shares (issue #3521). It sits at this rung because `cli:Plan` is the lowest one: `cli:Assess`, `cli:Release` and `cli:Rehearse` are engine and reference downward to it, where a shared class in the surface module `cli:Command` would have made all three reference upward (rule 3).

Authority.purpose: External human/policy execution authority shared by release and recovery: a separate actor-bound Ed25519 trust root, an explicitly synchronized target-authoritative policy, exact expiring operation envelopes, stable target identity, and target-private one-time consumption/completion evidence.

Refresh.purpose: The B/P/W refresh planner, field diff and local state materializer that reconciles git, production and working state.

Environment.purpose: The environment registry and lifecycle that materialize, bind and reap the environments the orchestrator drives.

Recovery.purpose: Rollback authority and the verified/scoped rollback profiles that prove a target can be returned to a known state, plus profile selection, checkpoint inventory/retention, literal recovery claims, and immutable preparation/outcome documents for actor-authorized asynchronous recovery.

Onboarding.purpose: Adopting, initializing, diagnosing and triaging a site — including canonical connection and Git-handoff receipts at the first-run boundary.

Adapter.purpose: Authoring-side adapter tooling: catalog, draft, observation, manifest validation against the agent's policy, the operator's own Ed25519 certification authority (keygen/certify/pin), `lint-tree` -- the WordPress-free half of the suspicious-reference linter, which replays a recorded lint environment into the engine's own Lint::scan_tree() -- `boundary`, the version-range bisector, which reads a recorded release list plus an accumulating probe-outcome table and emits package-owned artifact rows as EVIDENCE, never a manifest edit, and `proposals`, the scheduled job around that planner: it re-bisects every pinned plugin from its own recorded ledger, emits the range bump as BOTH edits in the Canon-byte-equal shape ManifestDispositions.php:632-637 demands, and derives a per-adapter last_verified that deliberately lives outside manifests/ (a byte there is adapter identity, so storing freshness beside a manifest would re-pin the fleet on every re-verification). WP-5.6 adds `distribution`: `discover|install|update` over a wprism-adapter-index/v1 pointer document, the only verbs in this module with a transport at all -- digest-pinned resolution that never falls through, verification in a staging root through the agent's own AdapterCertification::verifyFile(), and a package that lands as the two files certify already writes, so the engine cannot tell it from a hand-placed adapter.

Code.purpose: Host-side code-half sourcing: the wp.org release cache, fetch, verify, unpack and tree-digest primitives, the imported-archive store `wprism code-import` fills for components with no wp.org release, the locked / first-party / unsourced classification behind `wprism init` and `wprism code-classify`, and the lock resolver `wprism code-resolve` materializes with.

Command.purpose: The `wprism` verb handlers, agent passthrough, option parsing, preflight and operator output. Composition across engine modules happens here: a `*Command` calls each engine module downward and hands the results to the next, which is why the populated cli modules need no intra-layer exceptions.

Assess.purpose: The assess mechanism — stack inventory and the authority block, the per-surface catalog carrying the six spec dimensions, the closed gap-action set, the `wprism-assess-report/v1` document and its bounded human renderer. Mechanism only: `AssessCommand` (cli:Command) calls Doctor, the environment registry and the adapter catalog and hands their results in as data, which is what keeps this module free of intra-layer and upward edges (module map rule 9). `FleetCensus` is the one file here with no target at all: it folds N `wprism-assess-inventory/v1` documents into `wprism-fleet-census/v1` against a manifest library on this machine, which is why it reaches agent:Policy (the reviewed-claim projector) and agent:Review (the one option-prefix grammar the residual is grouped in) as data sources rather than through any cli module. `CohortRebaseline` (WP-6.3) is one level further out and reaches nothing at all: it folds TWO census documents into `wprism-cohort-rebaseline/v1` — the coverage-ratio delta, the funnel movement and the per-adapter surface attribution a cohort's exit criterion reads — so its only inputs are documents `FleetCensus` already published, and it depends on that class alone.

Release.purpose: The release mechanism — `SourceStageReceipt` durably binds an inert Git source stage and `ReleasePrepare` binds that receipt, authority/capability policy identities and the exact externally-authorizable plan bytes; `AuthorizationPlan` builds, freezes, digests and re-verifies `wprism-authorization-plan/v1`; `AuthorizationPlanRenderer`, `ReleaseOutcome`, `ReleaseOperationStatus`, `NextAction` and `JourneyOracle` own its bounded presentation, terminal outcome, monotonic operation-status and verification contracts. Mechanism only: the verb boundaries (`StageSourceCommand`, `ReleaseCommand`, `VerifyCommand`, `RecoverCommand`, cli:Command) compose it with Authority, Environment, Recovery and the existing promote/deploy handlers.

Rehearse.purpose: The rehearsal mechanism — `RehearsalPlanPreview`, which joins the converged environment's plan-category projection with the assess-style surface rows restricted to that plan's actual scope to state what a release would touch, and `RehearsalDisclosure`, which owns MUP §2.2's containment banner and its consequence. Mechanism only, and pure: no I/O, no clock, no provider. The verb boundary (`RehearseCommand`, cli:Command) drives `EnvironmentLifecycle` and hands both documents in as data, which is what keeps this module free of intra-layer and upward edges (module map rule 9).

Contract.purpose: The per-site application contract as one object — manifests, site policy, evidence pins, bindings and capability report composed and addressable — plus `ProjectionVocabulary`, the single implementation of the spec-word projection that Assess, Release and Rehearse all read. Pure and offline-testable: a document, not a session.

not_moved.cli/wprism: stays at cli/wprism (the executable); its require list is rewritten by the codemod
